Smt. Jaya Rahul Avhad And Another vs State Of U.P. on 18
September, 2023
Author: Shekhar Kumar Yadav

Bench: Shekhar Kumar Yadav
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:179340
Court No. - 71
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 9394 of 2023
Applicant :- Smt. Jaya Rahul Avhad And Another

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Rishabh Agrawal,Madhukar Maurya
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Anurag Vajpeyi,Syed Imran Ibrahim
Hon'ble Shekhar Kumar Yadav,J.
1.

Heard Mr. Rishabh Agrawal and Madhukar Maurya, learned counsel for the applicants, Mr.
Vedmani Tiwari, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and Syed Imran Ibrahim,
learned counsel for the informant.
2. This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No.193 of 2022, under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 IPC, Police Station Noida Sector-58,
District Gautambuddh Nagar.

sentences.text: In short, the prosecution story is that the applicants told the business plan to the informant if he invest Rs.2.5 crore rupees, he will get Rs. 97.5 lakh per month for a period of ten months and regarding that an agreement was made between the parties.
It is further alleged that Rs.2.5 crore has been transferred through RTGS/NEFT and 10 post dated cheques were given by the applicants to the informant.

It is further alleged that out of Rs.2.5 crore, the applicants have given a cheque amounting to Rs.97.5 lakh to the informant, which was dishonoured, thereafter, the applicants have paid Rs.97.5 lakh in the account of informant's company.
It is further alleged that rest of money was not paid by the applicants to the informant.
4. Learned counsel for the applicants have submitted that the applicants are innocent and have been falsely implicated in the present case.
The impugned FIR has been lodged through an application under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C. after two and half years of the alleged incident for which no plausible explanation has been mentioned.

The amount as alleged in the impugned FIR was taken as a lone and not taken for such purpose even the informant did not produce any evidence regarding his claim that applicants made promise to pay Rs.97.5 lakh per month for a period of 10 months.
He has further submitted that the dispute is purely civil in nature but has given criminal colour just to pressurize the applicants.
The applicants have not committed any cheating with the informant and in case there is any grievance of the informant, he may file recovery suit against the applicants.
No offence under Sections 467, 468, 471 and 420 IPC is made out against the applicants.
He has further submitted that the investigation is going on and till date no charge sheet has been filed.
The applicants are having no previous criminal history as has been mentioned in paragraph 33 of the affidavit.

5. Learned counsel for the applicants have further submitted that due to the aforesaid reason, the applicants have apprehension of imminent arrest and in case, the applicants are released on anticipatory bail, they will not misuse the liberty and would co-operate with the trial.

In support of his submission, he he relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mohd. Ibrahim and others vs. State of Bihar and another and Ramesh Kumar vs. State of NCT of Delhi, AIR Online 2023 SC 530.
6.

entities.text: Mohd. Ibrahim and others vs. State of Bihar and another and Ramesh Kumar vs. State of NCT of Delhi, AIR Online 2023 SC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the applicants and has prayed for rejection by submitting that the applicants are having criminal history of three cases, which is of the same nature and habitual of committing such type of offene.
Applicants
have taken money of Rs.2.5 crores from the informant.
They have issued a cheque which was also dishonoured and after dishonour of the first cheque, the applicants have given Rs.97.5 lakh to the informant.
Rest amount has not been given to the informant, hence, the applicants have committed forgery as well as cheating against the informant.
They have further submitted that in the Declaration-cum-undertaking form, there is no signature of the informant.
They have further submitted that the allegations are very serious and in view of the seriousness of the allegations made against the applicants, they are not entitled to grant of anticipatory bail.
The apprehension of the applicants is not founded on any material on record.

Only on the basis of imaginary fear,
anticipatory bail cannot be granted.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent of accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate entire available material against the accused carefully and that the exact role of the accused has also to be taken into consideration.

entities.text: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In Subramanian Swamy Vs. C.B.I., (2014) 8 SCC 682, the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that corruption is an enemy of the nation and tracking down corrupt public servants and punishing such persons is a necessary mandate of the 1988 Act.

9. In P. Chidambaram Vs. Director Of Enforcement reported in (2019) 9 SCC 24, the Apex Court has clearly held that grant of anticipatory bail particularly in economic offences would definitely hamper the effective investigation.

entities.text: P. Chidambaram Vs. Director Of Enforcement reported in (2019) 9 SCC 24
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the cases of corruption the custodial interrogation of an accused is necessary because he/she may provide the information leading to discovery of material fact and relevant information.
10. The anticipatory bail can be granted only in exceptional circumstances where the court is prima facie of the view that the applicants have falsely been enroped in the offence.
Being an extraordinary remedy, it should be restored to only in a special case.
11. From the perusal of material on record and looking into the facts of the case, prima facie offence is made out against the applicants.
It would be inappropriate to discuss the evidence at this stage because it is likely to influence the trial court.

12. In the light of above, looking to the facts and circumstances of this case, submissions of learned counsel for the parties as mentioned above, taking into consideration the role assigned to the applicants as per prosecution case, gravity and nature of accusation, this Court is of the view that no case for exercising its discretionary power under Section 438 Cr.P.C. is made out in favour of applicants.
13. Accordingly, this application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. is dismissed.
Order Date :- 18.9.2023
